data.title: Clover Posts Strong Phase 2 Data for Combination Respiratory Vaccines in Older Adults
data.description:
Clover Biopharmaceuticals Ltd. ( (HK:2197) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Clover Biopharmaceuticals reported positive preliminary Phase 2 data from an Australian trial of its combination respiratory vaccines SCB-1022 and SCB-1033 in adults aged 60 to 85. The vaccines, targeting RSV, hMPV and PIV3, generated robust neutralizing antibody responses comparable to or higher than prior early-stage data, without diminished responses in participants over 75 years.

The trial also showed about a 62% reduction in reported respiratory tract infections in vaccinated groups versus placebo over 28 days, during a period of notable RSV circulation alongside hMPV and PIV in Australia. Both candidates were generally well-tolerated with mostly mild, transient adverse events, and Clover has successfully scaled up commercial production of key antigens to 2,000L, reducing development risk and supporting potential mid- to late-stage trials and partnership discussions.

data.title: Kangqiao Service Group Faces Setback as Supreme People’s Court Upholds Loan Judgment
data.description:
Kangqiao Service Group Limited ( (HK:2205) ) has shared an announcement.

Kangqiao Service Group Limited has provided an update on ongoing litigation involving its wholly owned subsidiary, Kangqiao Yueshenghuo Service Group Co., Ltd., relating to irregularities previously discovered in the subsidiary’s bank accounts and associated loan and collateral arrangements. The case centers on a Second Civil Judgment in China, which the company had sought to challenge through a retrial application to the Supreme People’s Court.

The Supreme People’s Court has now dismissed the subsidiary’s retrial application, finding that the evidence submitted on the alleged invalidity of the loan contracts and a promissory letter did not qualify as new evidence sufficient to overturn the original ruling. The court also held that arguments about connected guarantees and listing-rule-related disclosure and approval procedures lacked legal basis, and that the lending bank had carried out appropriate review and was not acting in bad faith.
